title: The evidence leans to a night of decree

points.label: A Christmas hymn
points.text: Luxenberg reads qadr through Syriac **ḥelqā, “fate”**, linked to a word for both “birth horoscope” and **Christmas**; shahr becomes “vigil”. Richard Bell had compared verse 5 with **Christmas Eve**.

points.label: Night of predestination
points.text: Sinai calls the Christmas step a **non sequitur** with no Syriac evidence, and notes anzala always sends down revelation. He reads a **“night of predetermination”**: an older night of fate, reinterpreted as the night revelation came down, like **44:3-4**.

points.label: Revelation in Ramadan
points.text: Ibn Kathir joins 97:1 with **2:185 and 44:3**: the night falls in **Ramadan**, when, per Ibn ʿAbbas, the whole Qur’an came down to the lowest heaven. Qatadah: the year’s matters are **“measured out”** then.
points.who: Ibn Kathir, citing Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah

bottom_text: Sinai’s critique leaves Luxenberg’s philology weak; “decree” fits 44:3-4 and Qur’anic usage. Yet Sinai grants a Christmas link can’t be dismissed outright, so an echo of Luke 2 stays open.
source_label: Sinai, Der Islam 88 (2012), pp. 13–19 · Ibn Kathir on 97
